questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: A cube is split into three congruent pyramids that share one vertex of the cube as their apex, as shown. Use this to explain why a pyramid's volume is ⅓Bh.
questions.prompt_markup: A cube is split into three congruent pyramids that share one vertex of the cube as their apex, as shown. Use this to explain why a pyramid's volume is ⅓Bh.
questions.correct_answer: Each pyramid has the cube's base B = s² and height h = s, and the three fill the cube, so each has volume ⅓s³ = ⅓Bh.
questions.required_method: Compare each pyramid's base and height with the cube's.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: three congruent pyramids fill the cube; each has base = a face (B = s²) and height = s; so V = ⅓s³ = ⅓Bh. Extension to other pyramids by Cavalieri (cross-sections scale the same way) earns full credit but is not required.

questions.prompt: Explain why the volume of a cone is ⅓πr²h, using pyramids.
questions.prompt_markup: Explain why the volume of a cone is ⅓πr²h, using pyramids.
questions.correct_answer: Pyramids with regular n-gon bases inscribed in the circle have V = ⅓Bh; as n grows, B approaches πr² and the pyramids approach the cone, so V = ⅓πr²h.
questions.required_method: Think of pyramids whose bases are regular polygons with more and more sides.
questions.grading_note: Any valid explanation. Essential: pyramid volume ⅓Bh; base polygons approach the circle (B → πr²); the pyramids approach the cone. Alternative: Cavalieri comparison with a pyramid of equal base area and height.
